title: Mixed-precision quant serving accuracy drift, OOM churn, and autoscaler thrash - action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a regional capacity change and model rollout, a mixed-precision execution path exposed a subtle numeric mismatch between int8 weights and fp16 attention kernels. This caused gradual token-level accuracy drift for several production models, which triggered canary alarms and a traffic shift. The increased tail latency and occasional OOMs caused Dedicated autoscaler thrash and a small number of 503s for enterprise tenants.
impact_summary: ~2% elevation in perplexity on canary prompts for 3 models, spike in per-request latency (95p from 110ms -> 380ms), autoscaler oscillation in eu-west region for ~46 minutes, ~7 customers saw degraded responses, no data leak or integrity loss.
timeline:
2026-02-18 09:12 UTC - Canary alert: canary model accuracy regression detected.
2026-02-18 09:15 UTC - Canary traffic cut to 10% and rollback attempted automatically (rollback failed due to variant mismatch).
2026-02-18 09:23 UTC - Observed increase in 95p latency and GPU memory fragmentation.
2026-02-18 09:30 UTC - Autoscaler increased fleet size twice, then decreased twice (oscillation) due to short-lived high memory churn.
2026-02-18 09:48 UTC - Several model worker pods entered OOM loop and restarted; brief 503s reported.
2026-02-18 10:05 UTC - Mitigation: forced traffic to fp16-only variant and temporarily disabled mixed-precision path for affected models.
2026-02-18 10:22 UTC - Latency and errors returned to baseline.
2026-02-19 - Investigation started; reproducer created on dedicated QA with same model and synthetic load.
2026-03-02 - Root-cause validated: kernel precision mismatch + KV-cache offset handling bug when switching precision on warm cache.
root_cause: Two faults combined: (1) A precision promotion path introduced during the mixed-precision rollout caused attention kernels to use fp16 assumptions while the quantized int8 weight access still used int8 dequant semantics, producing slight numerical drift manifesting under certain prompt distributions. (2) A separate regression in KV-cache offset arithmetic when a model was served across precision boundaries produced transient memory fragmentation and occasional oversubscription leading to OOMs. The autoscaler reacted to transient memory signals and created short-lived nodes, causing capacity thrash.
immediate_remediations: 1) Reverted mixed-precision runtime flag for affected model family to force fp16-only execution. 2) Hotfix to disable the precision transition codepath in the serving runtime (rolled within 30m). 3) Scoped autoscaler threshold to ignore OOM spikes below 90s to prevent oscillation. 4) Expanded canary checks to include a token-level perplexity test and KV-cache pressure metric.
long_term_mitigations:
1) Implement a formal precision-compatibility test suite that runs int8/fp16/fp32 crosschecks with representative prompt sets in CI.
2) Add runtime invariant checks for KV-cache offsets when a precision transition occurs; fail-fast and fallback to a stable variant.
3) Introduce graceful-degradation policy: on detected numeric drift beyond threshold, automatically route to the verified fp16-only variant and mark the mixed-precision variant as 'degraded'.
4) Improve autoscaler hysteresis and add memory-fragmentation signals to prevent thrash during warmups.
5) Conduct a dedicated load test with warm caches and precision switches in staging every week for the next quarter.

notes: This incident highlights a class of regressions that only appear when precision transitions occur with warm KV caches. Cross-team coordination between Research and Runtime is required to prevent recurrence. The rollout gating checklist will be updated to include numeric crosschecks and KV-cache pressure testing.
